intentions.title: Maintain ONE block-tree document model (PortableDoc) that every surface — API, Studio editor, TUI/Go pdrender, email — reads and writes without drift
intentions.evidence: render.ex explicitly ties its Pd-tree walk to the Go twin in internal/pdrender via shared golden fixtures (internal/pdrender/testdata/golden/); patch.ex's six ops are pinned by golden fixtures under api/test/support/fixtures/doc-patch-op/ that double as the cross-surface op contract for CLI/SDK/Studio; render.ex module doc states output must be byte-identical across renderer refactors (v1/v2/v3 body_html_render_version stamping + mix barkpark.rehydrate_body_html).

intentions.title: Let legacy schema-bound documents (Classic content[fieldName]) and the new free-form block/body model coexist with zero data migration and no drift between them
intentions.evidence: projection.ex: bound blocks (carrying fieldName) project into content[fieldName] so existing Classic queries read unchanged; free blocks fold into content['body']; project/3 or project/4 is declared the SOLE writer of those keys ('no-drift guarantee'); synthesis.ex lazily synthesizes a block list in memory for legacy docs with no content['blocks'] yet, with a documented no-rewrite invariant (synthesize -> Projection.project round-trips byte-equal).

intentions.title: Provide a pure, side-effect-free patch engine (append/insert/patch/replace/remove/move) as the single owner of block-tree mutation semantics
intentions.evidence: patch.ex module doc: 'apply_patch/2 is pure: it never mutates its input, performs no Repo access, no GenServer, no I/O... never a silent no-op, never a partially-applied result'; defines six ops with structured error tuples (:block_not_found, :type_mismatch, :duplicate_id, :locked_block, :constraint, :invalid_op); enforces template-lock and constraint-vocabulary backstops before mutating.

intentions.title: Enforce a composition doctrine — element/widget/section tiers and structural constraint declarations — so document types can pin required layout shape without ad hoc validation code scattered across the app
intentions.evidence: tiers.ex classifies every renderable block type into :element/:widget/:section with a hard-invariant test that fails if any renderer-producible type is unclassified; constraints.ex implements presence/cardinality/position/relation declarations matched by role-or-type OR tier atom, explicitly kept Content/DB-free ('layering purity'); slots.ex builds the typed-slot model for widgets on top of Tiers.tier_of/1 as the single canonical classifier.

intentions.title: Support incremental adoption of the slot-native widget model (e.g. callout, card) without breaking byte-identical output for legacy inline-encoded widgets
intentions.evidence: slots.ex documents callout's dual-write compat: legacy {'type':'callout','content':[...]} is normalized to/from a slots.body[0] paragraph so both encodings render the identical PdText, while 'card' is the first genuinely slots-native widget with no legacy inline form and its own flattening contract (card_body_text/1) that the Go/email renderers don't yet support (filed follow-up).

intentions.title: Give authored papers live, always-current views of external task data (bp tasks) without persisting resolved snapshots into the document's saved source of truth
intentions.evidence: task_resolver.ex resolve/2 replaces a block's `query` with a fetched `snapshot`/`task`/aggregate for read-time rendering via an injected fetch function (no direct DB dependency), while preview/2 is a separate, non-mutating channel specifically so the Studio editor's continuous-save diff never persists stale resolved rows (doctrine D5/D3 byte-stability); also resolves dataviz aggregates (chart/heatmap/stat) via an optional agg_fetch, degrading gracefully offline.

intentions.title: Render one authoritative HTML representation of a document across radically different delivery contexts (email HTML, standalone article export, embedded fragment) from a single walker, honoring theming, wikilinks, embeds, live valuerefs, and encrypted-field redaction
intentions.evidence: render.ex render_html/2 threads :style (:email vs :article), :theme (palette_for/2), :wikilinks, :embeds, and :values maps into the walk, all opt-in and byte-identical when absent; document/2 wraps :article output with the compile-time-inlined Stylesheet.css() for CSP-safe standalone export while :email keeps a byte-frozen fully-inline wrapper for Outlook; render_block/2 redacts FieldCipher-encrypted values before render so ciphertext or plaintext never leaks into the body_html cache or PubSub deltas.
